requirement:
The adapter's observation callback receives the selected identity and the
parsed source snapshot. `ToolAgent` records any dependency it returns when
those contents are delivered, under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.provider_observations`.
The callback maps the source item into the application's graph: a node
dependency records its identity and the fingerprint of the supplied contents.
That dependency becomes stale when the node's fingerprint changes. A callback
returning `None` supplies no dependency; calling `SourceAnalysis::parse`
directly also records none. Dependency comparison follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
rationale:
I judged the tests adequate for `requirements.sdk.graph.context-tools.read_source.inputs`. I did not read `record_is_current` or `Memory`, so I am assuming the staleness check does what its name and use in the test suggest.

All tests below are in `crates/habeas-sdk/tests/agent.rs`.

- **The callback receives the selected identity and the parsed snapshot.**
  - `source_reads_track_optional_dependencies_and_empty_searches_remain_discovery` asserts inside the callback that the resource location is `note.txt` and the selector is `""`. It also reads the parsed source text.
  - `source_tools_forward_arguments_and_present_discovery_and_read_results` records the ids the callback sees. They are `""`, `""` and `fn[chosen]` for the omitted, empty and explicit selectors. It also asserts the parsed text.
  - `cached_selected_source_reads_record_exact_delivered_contents_and_errors_add_no_input` resolves `id.selector` against `parsed.outline` inside the callback.

- **`ToolAgent` records the returned dependency when the contents are delivered.**
  - `source_tools_keep_search_discovery_separate_from_delivered_source_reads` checks that the inspection holds exactly one `Dependency::Node(Node(7), …)`. Its fingerprint value is the delivered text. The preceding `search_text` call adds nothing.
  - `source_read_pages_retain_text_and_dependencies_without_another_read` checks that paged delivery carries the dependency and that the callback runs only once.
  - `source_tools_forward_arguments_and_present_discovery_and_read_results` asserts that `delivery.dependencies` holds the expected fingerprint for each selector.

- **A node dependency records its identity and the fingerprint of the supplied contents.** The tests assert `Node(7)`, the scheme, and a value equal to either the full text or the selected node's lines. The cached-provider test asserts the exact value `fn observed() { call(); }`. Its graph holds different current text, so the fingerprint can only come from the delivered snapshot. A missing selector (`fn[missing]`) adds no extra dependency.

- **The dependency becomes stale when the node's fingerprint changes.** In `source_reads_track_optional_dependencies_and_empty_searches_remain_discovery`, `record_is_current` returns true on unchanged graph contents. After the graph contents change, it returns false when a dependency was recorded and true when none was.

- **A callback returning `None` supplies no dependency.** The same test runs with `record_dependency` false and asserts `record.dependencies.is_empty()`.

- **`SourceAnalysis::parse` called directly records none.** The same test calls `factory.analysis.parse(...)` directly. It then asserts that the inspection's dependencies are empty and that the callback count is 0.

- **Dependency comparison follows `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.** This is a citation, so it needs no test here. The staleness assertions above exercise it anyway.

I found no untested obligation and no marking gap, and no `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply.

The tracked inspection context records successful source-node reads delivered
to the procedure as assessment dependencies, whether the provider uses defaults
or overrides. Each fingerprint describes the contents delivered to the caller.
:::{req} checking_records
```rust,ignore
// Method on Validator<D>.
/// Compare each recorded input with the current domain state.
/// Return true when every fingerprint still matches, including an empty trace.
pub fn check_inputs<O>(
&self,
inputs: &Fingerprinted<D, O>,
) -> Result<bool, D::Error>;
The method resolves the recorded dependencies through graph operations and
fingerprinting, comparing each with its saved observation. A fingerprint
mismatch returns `Ok(false)` and permits an early return; it need not resolve
later dependencies. An encountered dependency-resolution failure returns an
error.
It uses the current state that the caller intends to inspect, rather than
reusing source snapshots from an earlier invocation without establishing that
they remain current. These reads are separate from a criterion execution's
dependency trace.
Freshness checking has a separate observation scope from execution. Reads used
only to check old evidence do not become dependencies of the new result. A
checked snapshot can be reused if it still represents the current state; when
execution explicitly reads or delivers it, its fingerprint enters the new trace.
